## Unique objective
Make Deep actively distribute meaningful LTZZZ work to the two paid relay seats according to demonstrated model strengths, instead of leaving them idle, treating them as backup-only, or routing all work to domestic models. Build a repeatable skill-based routing and feedback loop using the existing Task Hub and relay-issue-run workflow. Do not create a parallel queue.

## Routing profile
- relay Claude (current evidenced candidate: claude-sonnet-4-6): prioritize code implementation, multi-file refactors, bug root-cause analysis, code review, test authoring, repository-wide context synthesis, technical documentation and implementation plans that need close code-to-spec consistency.
- relay GPT (current evidenced candidate: gpt-6.1-sol): prioritize complex task decomposition, architecture and interface planning, structured reasoning, competing-solution analysis, test strategy, CI/failure analysis, threat-model review using public_distributable inputs, and evidence-based acceptance audits.
- Combined high-impact workflow: Deep owns task decomposition/coordination; route Claude implementation and GPT independent architecture review, or reverse the roles when codebase evidence favors it. Reviews are advisory inputs, not approval gates. Do not wait for either seat before unrelated work proceeds.
- Deep should select the model/seat per task based on task type, context length, observed quality, latency, actual usage and cost evidence; allow short, interactive, long-context and batch calls where the current owner policy permits.

## Required work
1. Read current main and reconcile config/relay-seat-policy.json, config/deep-superagent.json, config/dispatch-seat-policy-20261117.json, relay-issue-run workflow, Task Hub routing and current Owner authority. Identify stale restrictions such as batch_only, execution-only/no-review wording, old balance-close semantics, or required peer review that conflict with Owner's current instructions.
2. Implement the minimum policy/code/docs/tests changes so relay Claude and relay GPT can be selected for substantive work by task type. Do not disable or auto-close a seat because balance is unknown/low; Owner will top up when needed. Do not claim a model call succeeded unless actual provider/model, request_id, HTTP, usage and receipt evidence exist.
3. Keep existing per-call/daily/project spend ceilings and no-auto-topup controls unchanged unless a separate explicit budget authorization is recorded. Balance availability is not a reason to remove the seats from routing or stop other tasks.
4. Route at least one suitable real, non-sensitive, non-reserved engineering task to each relay seat through the existing issue bridge; collect separate real call receipts and concrete deliverables (PR, review findings, test plan or implementation artifact). No dummy ping as the only proof.
5. Add a lightweight scorecard: task category, routed seat/model, output usefulness, factual/code defects found, revision count, latency, usage/cost and accepted artifact. Use it to improve future routing; do not treat one failed call as a permanent seat disable.
6. Preserve model identity distinctions: APIsRouter is a third-party relay, not official OpenAI/Anthropic direct access. Record actual_provider/model from receipts; unavailable stays unavailable.

## Allowed scope
Ordinary routing policy, task dispatch, prompt templates, code/docs/tests, relay issue labels/workflow integration, protected secret references and non-secret operational telemetry. Use only public_distributable project inputs for relay calls unless the applicable data-processing permission is already verified.

## Forbidden scope
No funds transfer, refund-finality action, signing, private-key/seed/root-key use, wallet or five-signature Safe operation. Do not expose secrets, tokens, passwords, customer personal/payment data or unapproved cross-border data. Do not increase spend ceilings, enable auto-topup, or claim official-provider identity. Do not create a parallel Task Hub or require GPT PASS/peer approval for ordinary work.

## Acceptance evidence
- Policy/config diff and regression tests show no balance-based seat closure and no batch-only gate where current Owner policy allows all request lengths.
- Routing matrix and prompt templates map work categories to relay Claude/GPT with a documented fallback that does not disable the other seat or unrelated queues.
- At least one substantive task per relay seat has a real call receipt with actual_provider/model, request_id, HTTP, usage, latency, cost and evidence path, plus a useful artifact/result.
- GitHub PR, head SHA, required CI jobs/steps, merge SHA (if merged), deployment workflow/source_commit/target/health/receipt (if deployment applies). No deployment claim without readback.
- Append-only scorecard and execution receipt linked to this original Task ID.
- Report remaining technical blocks precisely; a missing balance/call must not become a project-wide stop.

## Stop conditions
Stop only the specific call/action if an existing budget gate refuses it, input classification is not permitted, or one of the five reserved categories is implicated. Continue all other non-conflicting engineering and routing work.
